title: You almost missed her.
paragraphs: Not because she wasn’t there—but because she didn’t stand where the spotlight usually falls.

You remember the bold preacher. The one who spoke with fire, who carried Scripture in his mouth like a sword. His name was Apollos. Eloquent. Mighty in the Scriptures. The kind of man people would stop and listen to.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Before the crowds, before the clarity, before the fullness of truth—he was incomplete.
And God didn’t send an apostle to correct him.
God sent a woman most people overlook.

Apollos is preaching boldly in Ephesus. Passion is there. Knowledge is there. But something is missing. The message is accurate—but not complete. He knows the baptism of John, but not the fullness of Christ.
And in the crowd… she hears it.
Priscilla doesn’t interrupt him. She doesn’t shame him. She doesn’t build a platform off correcting him publicly.
“When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately.” (Acts 18:26)
She didn’t need a microphone to change a destiny.
You’ve been trained to celebrate the visible voices.

The ones with platforms.
The ones with crowds.
The ones with titles.
But heaven… pays attention to something else.
Priscilla wasn’t writing epistles like Paul. She wasn’t leading public revivals.
But she shaped a man who would.
A teacher… who shaped a great preacher.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.
You’ve underestimated what God could do through you… because no one is applauding you.
Every time you held truth but stayed silent out of fear.
Every time you knew someone was walking in partial truth—but you didn’t step in with love and clarity.
Priscilla understood something many still don’t.
Truth is too important to be withheld just because it’s inconvenient to deliver.
But she also understood how to deliver it.
But to complete someone’s understanding of Christ.
That’s the difference between pride and discipleship.
Her name often appears before her husband’s.
And the people listening to him would inherit that same incompleteness.
One quiet conversation… changed the trajectory of many.
You don’t need a stage to shape someone.
And you need to care more about someone’s soul than your own comfort.
Because partial truth is still dangerous.
And someone in your life right now…
Speaking—but not fully aligned with Christ.
God didn’t let you hear it by accident.
There are voices rising right now who sound powerful—but are missing the center: Jesus Christ.
“...that in all things He might have the preeminence.” (Colossians 1:18)
If He is not central—the message is not complete.
So now you’re standing where she stood.
Stay silent… and let incomplete truth spread.
Or step in—wisely, humbly, privately if needed—and bring clarity that leads to life.
But to point them fully to Christ.
Say it plainly: “Lord, make me faithful with truth.”
There’s someone you already have in mind. You didn’t think of them randomly.
Follow this journey if you want to grow deeper—not just louder.
And if you’re ready to go beyond surface-level faith into real discipleship—where Scripture confronts, transforms, and builds you—step into it here:
Might depend on whether you speak.
